'''Giovanni Fabrizio''' "'''Nanni'''" '''Bignami''' ({{IPA|it|dʒoˈvanni faˈbrittsjo biɲˈɲaːmi}}; 10 April 1944 – 24 May 2017)<ref name=CTA/><ref name=LAR>{{cite news| url=http://www.repubblica.it/scienze/2017/05/25/news/addio_a_giovanni_bignami_astrofisico_e_divulgatore-166344330/| title=Morto Giovanni Bignami, astrofisico e divulgatore| last=Fraioli| first=Luca| work=[[la Repubblica]]| date=25 May 2017| accessdate=17 June 2017| language=it| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170619150925/http://www.repubblica.it/scienze/2017/05/25/news/addio_a_giovanni_bignami_astrofisico_e_divulgatore-166344330/| archive-date=19 June 2017| url-status=live}}</ref> was an Italian [[astrophysicist]], best known for his discovery of the [[neutron star]] [[Geminga]]. From March 2007 until August 2008, he was Chairman of the [[Italian Space Agency]]. Between 2010 and 2014, he was the first Italian to chair the [[Committee on Space Research]] (COSPAR), and from 2011 until 2015, he was President of [[INAF]]. He was also the chairman of the SKA project.<ref name=SKA>{{cite news| url=http://skatelescope.org/news/chairman-of-the-ska-board-prof-giovanni-bignami-passes-away/| title=Chairman Of The SKA Board Prof. Giovanni Bignami Passes Away| publisher=SKA Organisation| date=25 May 2017| accessdate=17 June 2017| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170607061849/http://skatelescope.org/news/chairman-of-the-ska-board-prof-giovanni-bignami-passes-away/| archive-date=7 June 2017| url-status=live}}</ref> He was married to fellow Italian astrophysicist [[Patrizia Caraveo]].<ref name=LPP/><ref>{{cite web| url= http://www.foam13.it/eventi%20e%20personalita/2011%20Giovanni%20Bignami/Giovanni%20Bignami.htm| title= Giovanni Bignami| publisher= Foam 13| accessdate= 17 June 2017| archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20141204203818/http://www.foam13.it/eventi%20e%20personalita/2011%20Giovanni%20Bignami/Giovanni%20Bignami.htm| archive-date= 4 December 2014| url-status= dead}}</ref> The asteroid [[6852 Nannibignami]] was named in his honour.<ref name=LAR/>

==Career==
[[File:Giovanni Bignami, 2004 (cropped).jpg|thumb|180px|left|Bignami in 2004]]
Bignami graduated from the [[University of Milan]] in 1968 with a degree in physics. From 1988 to 1997, he was the Principal Investigator for the [[European Space Agency]]'s [[XMM-Newton]] mission, and was a professor of [[astronomy]] and [[astrophysics]] at the [[IUSS Pavia|IUSS]] in [[Pavia]].<ref name=CTA/><ref>{{cite web| url= http://www.iusspavia.it/rubrica.php?id=348| title= Giovanni Bignami allo IUSS| publisher= iusspavia.it| url-status= dead| archiveurl= https://web.archive.org/web/20140116124337/http://www.iusspavia.it/rubrica.php?id=348| archivedate= 16 January 2014| df= dmy-all}}</ref> He is most known for his discovery of the [[neutron star]] [[Geminga]].<ref>{{cite web| url= http://www.iasf-milano.inaf.it/Divulgazione/divulgazione.php?pg=gamma_gem&mn=gamma&lin=gamma_gem| title= Storia della scoperta di Geminga| publisher= [[INAF]]| accessdate= 17 June 2017| language= it| archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20170531224146/http://www.iasf-milano.inaf.it/Divulgazione/divulgazione.php?pg=gamma_gem&mn=gamma&lin=gamma_gem| archive-date= 31 May 2017| url-status= live}}</ref> From 2004 to 2007, he was President of the Space Science Advisory Committee (SSAC) of the European Space Agency, and from 2007 to 2008, he was Chairman of the Italian Space Agency.<ref name=CTA>{{cite web| url= https://www.cta-observatory.org/memory-prof-giovanni-bignami/| title= In Memory of Prof. Giovanni Bignami| date= 29 May 2017| publisher= [[Cherenkov Telescope Array]]| accessdate= 17 June 2017| archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20170713103127/https://www.cta-observatory.org/memory-prof-giovanni-bignami/| archive-date= 13 July 2017| url-status= live}}</ref> In 2010, he was elected President of the [[Committee on Space Research]] (COSPAR), the first Italian to hold this post. He served until 2014.<ref name=SKA/> From 2011 until 2015, Bignami served as president of [[INAF]].<ref name=LAR/>

Bignami stood as a [[Democratic Party (Italy)|Democratic Party]] candidate for [[North-West Italy (European Parliament constituency)|Lombardy, Piedmont, Aosta Valley and Liguria]] in the [[2009 European Parliament election]]. His campaign slogan was ''Più ricerca in Italia, più futuro in Europa'' ("More research in Italy, more future in Europe"); he was not elected.<ref>{{cite web| url=http://www.giovannibignami.it/html/proposta_per_europa.html| title=Una proposta per l'Europa| publisher=Giovanni Bignami| accessdate=17 June 2017| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111119220502/http://www.giovannibignami.it/html/proposta_per_europa.html| archive-date=19 November 2011| url-status=dead}}</ref>

Bignami received several honours, including the [[Bruno Rossi Prize]] from the [[American Astronomical Society]], the Blaise Pascal Medal for Astrophysics from the European Academy of Sciences and the Von Karman Award from the [[International Academy of Astronautics]].<ref name=CTA/> He was named Officier of the [[Légion d'Honneur]] and the [[Ordre national du Mérite]] in France, and was a member of the [[Accademia dei Lincei]]<ref name=LAR/> and of the [[French Academy of Sciences]]. He was named Officer of the [[Order of Merit of the Italian Republic]] in 2016.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.quirinale.it/onorificenze/insigniti/339991|title=Bignami Prof. Giovanni Fabrizio|language=it|work=Le onorificenze della Repubblica Italiana|publisher=[[President of Italy|Presidency of the Italian Republic]]|access-date=2026-02-21}}</ref>

Bignami was also a [[science communicator]], writing for ''[[Corriere della Sera]]'', ''[[La Repubblica]]'', ''[[Il Sole 24 Ore]]'', ''[[L'Espresso]]'' and ''[[Panorama (magazine)|Panorama]]'', as well as appearing regularly on the TV programme ''[[Superquark]]'' as the curator of a segment about astronomy.<ref name=LPP/><ref name=LAR/>

Bignami died on 24 May 2017 in [[Madrid]], Spain, struck by a sudden illness.<ref name=CTA/><ref name=LAR/><ref name=SKA/>

==Works==
* (it) ''La storia nello spazio'', Milan, Mursia, 2001, {{ISBN|88-425-2939-7}}.
* (it) ''L'esplorazione dello spazio. Alla scoperta del sistema solare'', Bologna, Il Mulino, 2006, {{ISBN|88-15-11404-1}}.
* (it) I marziani siamo noi. Un filo rosso dal Big Bang alla vita, Bologna, Zanichelli, 2010, {{ISBN|978-88-08-26156-4}}. Translated into English as ''We are the Martians'', [[Springer Science+Business Media|Springer]], Berlin, 2012
* (it) Cosa resta da scoprire, Milano, Mondadori, 2011, {{ISBN|978-88-04-61364-0}}. Ristampato nel 2012 nella serie bestseller “Oscar”. Translated into English as ''Imminent Science'', Springer, 2014
* (it) G. Bignami-Cristina Bellon, Il futuro spiegato ai ragazzi, Milano, Mondadori, 2012, {{ISBN|978-88-04-61681-8}}.
* (it) Il mistero delle sette sfere. Cosa resta da esplorare. Dalla depressione di Afar alle stelle più vicine, Milano, Mondadori, 2013, {{ISBN|978-88-04-63068-5}}. Translated into English as ''The Mystery of the Seven Spheres'', Springer, 2015
* A Scenario for Interstellar Exploration and Its Financing, Heidelberg, Springer Verlag, 2013, {{ISBN|88-47-05336-6}}.
* (it) G. Bignami-Andrea Sommariva, ''Oro dagli asteroidi e asparagi da Marte. Realtà e miti dell'esplorazione dello spazio'', Milan, Mondadori University, 2015, {{ISBN|978-88-6184-418-6}}.
* G. Bignami-Andrea Sommariva, The Future of Human Space Exploration, [[Macmillan Publishers|Macmillan]], 2016.
